tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no external capture.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching a file outside the owned list, changing production code with no tests, fewer than 4 new def test_..., no negative test (pytest.raises/assert-blocked/assert-failed), or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/media_gates.py
  tests/test_media_gates_integration.py
  tests/test_transfer_length_streams.py

THE BUG, with a real render's evidence. A correct 36-minute podcast render was blocked by the transfer-validation precondition MAP_PROGRAM_LENGTH_MISMATCH: map_total=2156.886542s program=2156.927333s delta=40.79ms. The check (in validate_transfer, around media_gates.py:1196-1214) fails when abs(edited_duration - map_total) * VIDEO_RATE > 1.0 (i.e. more than one 30fps video frame).

WHY IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE. map_total is derived from VIDEO frame counts (sum of piece frames / 30fps). But edited_duration = _media_duration(edited), which returns MAX over ALL streams of the packet span, i.e. max(video_span, audio_span). The audio is AAC: it pads to whole 1024-sample frames (21.33ms at 48kHz) and the mux adds container priming, up to ~2 AAC frames (42.66ms) of LEGITIMATE extra audio. So on a render whose VIDEO matches the map to the exact frame, the AUDIO stream is ~1-2 audio-frames longer and _media_duration returns that longer audio span, tripping a video-timeline check. The 40.79ms delta sits inside the 2-AAC-frame padding envelope while the video has ZERO drift.

THE FIX (reviewed and chosen over alternatives; implement THIS, not a blanket tolerance widening).

1. Split the length precondition by stream. Compute the VIDEO packet span and the AUDIO packet span of the edited program SEPARATELY (probe_streams already yields per-stream; get each stream's packet_bounds). Do not use max() for this check.

2. VIDEO vs map: compare the VIDEO packet span against map_total with the EXISTING tight tolerance (more than one video frame => FAIL). The map is a video timeline, so this is the honest comparison and it still catches the real 'frame-count vs container drift' failure class, which is always many frames. Keep the failure code MAP_PROGRAM_LENGTH_MISMATCH for the video case and keep reporting map_total, the video program duration, and delta_ms.

3. AUDIO length: add a SEPARATE check. The audio packet span must be within an AAC-padding-aware tolerance of map_total: allow the audio to EXCEED map_total by up to a named constant AAC_PADDING_TOLERANCE_S (set it to 2 AAC frames at 48kHz = 2048/48000 = 0.04267s, with a comment explaining priming+trailer padding), but a DEFICIT (audio shorter than the video map) beyond a small grace, or a surplus BEYOND that padding envelope, must FAIL with a distinct code like AUDIO_LENGTH_MISMATCH. This closes the gap that checking video-only would otherwise open: truncated or corrupt audio must not pass.

DO NOT choose the rejected alternative of simply widening the video tolerance to >2 frames: a real 1-missing-video-frame (33.33ms) stacked with 1 AAC padding frame (21.33ms) = 54.66ms would then pass and mask a genuine dropped frame. The whole point is to keep video tight and handle audio padding in its own dimension.

Do not touch the 40ms ANCHOR threshold, the anchors logic, or any other gate. Only the length precondition.

TESTS ARE THE DELIVERABLE TOO. In tests/test_transfer_length_streams.py prove, with mocked probe_streams / packet_bounds so no real media is needed: (1) the exact failing case from production (video span == map_total, audio span = map_total + 40.79ms) now PASSES because the audio surplus is within the AAC padding envelope and the video matches; (2) a REAL video drop (video span = map_total + 2 frames) still FAILS with MAP_PROGRAM_LENGTH_MISMATCH; (3) truncated audio (audio span = map_total - 200ms) FAILS with AUDIO_LENGTH_MISMATCH; (4) audio surplus far beyond padding (map_total + 500ms) FAILS. Mock, do not require ffmpeg.
